status: Executable teaching examples, not production-conformance claims

cases.title: 01 / Whiteboard sketch
cases.question: What are the main things in this discussion?
cases.explanation: Unspecified objects and named associations capture a conversation before tables, datatypes or deployment are chosen. The sketch look makes the drawing informal; it does not set maturity to draft.
cases.try: Add a Return object and a named association, without assigning a datatype or a location.
cases.limitation: This is a conceptual sketch, not an implemented schema.

cases.title: 02 / Business concepts
cases.question: What does one customer relate to?
cases.explanation: Conceptual entities describe business meaning. Endpoint marks express one customer per order and optional multiple orders or shipments on the opposite ends.
cases.try: Change a cardinality only after deciding its business meaning; do not infer it from sample row counts.
cases.limitation: The diagram asserts intended cardinalities, not database-enforced constraints.

cases.title: 03 / Logical relational schema
cases.question: Which fields reference which identifiers?
cases.explanation: The field-level references connect Order line to Orders and Orders to Customer. Key icons and shared semantic-domain bindings can exist before physical SQL datatypes are selected.
cases.try: Use the compact display policy to hide the fields; field endpoint identities remain in the resolved model.
cases.limitation: Datatypes and enforcement are deliberately undecided. This does not generate DDL.

cases.title: 04 / SQL object dependencies
cases.question: What could be affected by changing a SQL definition?
cases.explanation: Procedure, view and table definitions use the same card grammar. Dependency arrows describe required definitions; they do not assert copying, scheduling or execution.
cases.try: Add the supplied index definition to a separate access-path view, keeping its target dependency explicit.
cases.limitation: This is declared dependency information. SQL parsing and database reverse engineering are not implemented.

cases.title: 05 / Nested document structure
cases.question: What is embedded rather than independently stored?
cases.explanation: A collection shape contains an embedded contacts array whose item shape is a document. The required/optional and nullability assertions stay independent.
cases.try: Add an optional property to the contact item. Compare it with a nullable required property.
cases.limitation: This is a schematic shape view, not a complete JSON Schema validator or an automatically expanded JSON tree.

cases.title: 06 / Property-graph schema
cases.question: Can a relationship have properties of its own?
cases.explanation: The PURCHASED edge type has purchased_at and quantity properties. Its incident node types are shown explicitly, so an edge is not confused with a property-free line.
cases.try: Add a second graph-edge type with its own properties and endpoint types.
cases.limitation: This is an incidence-style schema drawing; it does not query or validate a live graph database.

cases.title: 07 / Key-value design
cases.question: What is the key, and what shape is its value?
cases.explanation: Separate the session identity, the key-value store and the value record. A companion wide-column view shows partition and clustering roles without treating them as ordinary foreign keys.
cases.try: Change the value shape without changing the key definition, then inspect the wide-column companion view.
cases.limitation: The reference renderer uses a generic key glyph. Exact partition/clustering roles are explicit in source and the resolved model, not unique rendered row glyphs yet.

cases.title: 08 / Domain discovery and binding
cases.question: Do differently named fields share the same meaning?
cases.explanation: Orders.customer_id has an established domain binding. Support.account_ref is only a candidate. A separate representation-binding object leaves the SQL type decision open.
cases.try: Review the candidate and, only when meaning is confirmed, change candidate_domain_match to uses_domain.
cases.limitation: Successful rendering does not approve a domain match, select a SQL engine or infer a datatype.

cases.title: 09 / Namespace organization
cases.question: Which schema contains these SQL objects?
cases.explanation: Tables and routines can belong to the same schema. Namespace-membership relationships say nothing by themselves about cloud location or physical storage.
cases.try: Build another view over the same Orders definition that selects its shard and deployed copies instead.
cases.limitation: This models declared membership, not a live catalogue inventory.

cases.title: 10 / Shards, copies and placement
cases.question: Which fragment is copied, and where are its copies?
cases.explanation: One logical Orders definition maps to a fragment. Two separate copies realize that fragment and sit on different services. A replication flow is distinct from the copy and placement relationships.
cases.try: Add another shard as a new fragment, rather than duplicating the business concept.
cases.limitation: This is a declared topology. Replica health, actual placements and delivery guarantees have not been observed.

cases.title: 11 / Data-flow diagram
cases.question: What data enters a process and what comes out?
cases.explanation: A dataset is consumed by a validation activity that writes another dataset. Movement arrows explain processing, not a foreign-key relationship.
cases.try: Add a rejected-record output as a distinct dataset with its own flow.
cases.limitation: This uses DDN process/data-flow conventions. It is not a claim of formal DFD or BPMN execution semantics.

cases.title: 12 / Event publication and consumers
cases.question: How can one change stream feed independent projections?
cases.explanation: Capture, transport, consumption and projection building are separate stages. History and search are independent derived representations with separate consumers.
cases.try: Add a consumer group and a stated delivery requirement; do not infer exactly-once effects from the Kafka label.
cases.limitation: This is an architectural contract illustration. The renderer does not operate Kafka, monitor lag or prove delivery behaviour.

cases.title: 13 / Dataset lineage
cases.question: Where did an analytical result come from?
cases.explanation: Declared derivation links connect the shared Orders table to daily totals and a dashboard. Unlike the operational flow view, this view does not claim a transfer mechanism or schedule.
cases.try: Reuse Orders in both a lineage view and a deployment view; its identity must remain the same.
cases.limitation: Lineage is authored information here, not automatically harvested or verified runtime provenance.

cases.title: 14 / Valid time and recorded time
cases.question: When did a fact apply, and when did we know it?
cases.explanation: A correction known on March 5 says suspension was effective from March 3. Three synthetic rows preserve the earlier recorded belief and the later corrected intervals. End bounds are exclusive; null in an end column means open-ended in this example.
cases.try: Compare the valid state on March 4 with what the warehouse knew on March 4. Do not substitute arrival time for business-effective time.
cases.limitation: These are civil-date examples with an explicit open-end convention. The renderer does not execute temporal queries or provide point-in-time restore.

cases.title: 15 / Dimensional warehouse
cases.question: What is the fact grain and which dimensions describe it?
cases.explanation: A central fact representation references customer, product and date dimensions. The note declares one row per order line so measures are interpreted at a known grain.
cases.try: Add a promotion dimension or bridge only after specifying its multiplicity and effect on the grain.
cases.limitation: The star arrangement is deliberately positioned in this teaching view. There is no automatic star-layout engine or measure-additivity validator.

cases.title: 16 / Vector and embedding lineage
cases.question: Which source and transformation produced these vectors?
cases.explanation: Source descriptions are consumed by an embedding activity that generates a vector representation. The transformation version and model version belong to the design metadata.
cases.try: Extend the view with a query interface or add feature and model-artifact kinds for an ML feature pipeline.
cases.limitation: This illustrates lineage; it does not run a model, calculate embeddings or assess model quality.

cases.title: 17 / Data products and contracts
cases.question: Which contract applies, and who stewards it?
cases.explanation: A data product conforms to a declared contract, and the contract has a responsible team. The relationship direction distinguishes the governed object from its policy or owner.
cases.try: Add separate product ownership and operational responsibility relationships rather than assuming contract stewardship covers both.
cases.limitation: The example documents responsibilities. It does not validate compliance or enforce a contract.

cases.title: 18 / Data handling boundaries
cases.question: What must happen before data leaves a restricted context?
cases.explanation: The declared process removes direct identifiers and aggregates contact records before an export. Scope frames separate the restricted source from a review-before-release context.
cases.try: Add explicit policy and approval records. Record which checks would support a release decision.
cases.limitation: The labels are a proposed handling design, not proof of anonymization, legal compliance or network enforcement. Frames alone do not implement security.

cases.title: 19 / Backup and restore design
cases.question: Which artifact is used to construct a recovery target?
cases.explanation: A backup artifact is the input to an isolated restore activity. The resulting database is a distinct target, not another drawing of the production database.
cases.try: Add a restore test, log coverage and recovery objectives before claiming a point-in-time recovery capability.
cases.limitation: No restore was performed. This backup-only example does not prove PITR, recoverability, RPO or RTO.

cases.title: 20 / Migration and target design
cases.question: How will the old representation become the new one?
cases.explanation: Legacy and target tables have distinct instance identities. Extraction and loading are connected through an explicit mapping/reconciliation activity; maturity indicators remain independent of drawing style.
cases.try: Add a parallel-run comparison, cutover decision and rollback path as explicit activities or constraints.
cases.limitation: The diagram documents a plan; it does not execute a migration or prove zero-downtime cutover.

cases.title: 21 / Example-driven data quality
cases.question: What is the expected outcome for a concrete invalid input?
cases.explanation: The input grid deliberately contains a null status. The expected grid excludes that row. Column bindings target the same status-record fields, so the fixture survives a display-name change.
cases.try: Change one input record and explicitly update or reject the expected output. A sample is not automatically a constraint.
cases.limitation: The reference renderer displays the fixture but does not execute the validation. Test-runner integration is a separate task.

cases.title: 22 / Navigable design documentation
cases.question: How can a document offer an overview without repeating the entire model?
cases.explanation: An overview links to detailed logical and business views. Each target view selects shared data and policies independently. The reference cards represent navigation, not new datasets or copies.
cases.try: Open the exported SVG directly and follow a detail link, or use the companion links below the image. The same file defines both destinations.
cases.limitation: Links inside an SVG shown as an ordinary image are not interactive. Companion HTML links provide the portable fallback. Existing core examples separately demonstrate inline subdiagrams.
